name: Rhinoplasty simulation apps

card.summary: Morphing and 3D-imaging tools that preview how a nose might look after surgery; used by clinics and by prospective patients, with outcomes that are not guaranteed.
card.note: A simulated preview is an illustration, not a promise of surgical result.

quick.overview:
Rhinoplasty simulation software lets a person or a surgeon alter a photo or 3D scan of a nose to show a proposed change. Clinics use 3D cameras and planning software during consultations, and consumer apps offer similar photo morphing.

The topic appears in looksmaxxing discussion as a way to preview a result before surgery. This article is short because the available sources describe the clinical use only briefly.
quick.mechanism: Software maps the nose from standard photographs or 3D camera captures and lets the operator reshape contours digitally, so patient and surgeon can discuss the planned change.
quick.risks: The tools themselves are low-risk. The surgical result can differ from a simulation because healing, swelling and tissue behaviour vary between individuals; swelling after rhinoplasty can take a year or more to fully settle.

lead: Rhinoplasty simulation apps and software let people preview how a nose might look after surgery, or after different changes to its shape, by editing a photo or a 3D model. The point is to see a proposed profile or tip before committing, and to give surgeon and patient a shared picture of the target.

Surgical references describe 3D simulations and planning that can communicate the patient's existing deformities and the planned approach, and 3D cameras that capture, inspect, analyse and modify the nose so a potential result can be shown to the patient [1].

Clinical systems of this kind sit alongside consumer apps that morph a photo. They belong to the wider field of computer-aided surgical simulation, in which specialized software renders a virtual 3D model of the patient and simulates intervention before surgery [2].

chain: Photo or 3D scan of the nose
Preview of a potential result to guide the decision and plan
angle.text: A preview helps a person decide what change to ask for, whether it suits the face, and communicate it to a surgeon. Previews are visual predictions and are not a guarantee of the surgical outcome.

infobox: Photos from several angles or a 3D camera capture [1]

paras: Rhinoplasty references describe software-based 3D simulation as a way to show existing deformities and plan the proposed approach, and 3D cameras as a way to inspect the nose and edit it virtually so both parties can discuss a likely outcome [1].
Pre-operative consultation also includes a history, an exam of skin type, symmetry, valves and septum, and photographs from several angles, which supply the images these tools work from [1].

Healing differs between people and swelling can take at least a year to fully diminish, which is relevant to how closely a preview resembles a final result [1]. Wikipedia cites revision surgery as needed in roughly 5 to 20 percent of rhinoplasties, while flagging that the article needs more citations [1].

Wikipedia describes the general approach as using specialized software to render a patient's gathered data as a virtual 3D model, with surgical intervention simulated before surgery. It cites maxillofacial examples such as bone segment navigation in orthognathic surgery and mid-face reconstruction; it does not address cosmetic nose previews specifically [2].
